title: Find the missing note
hook: Cover it and rebuild its three fields: how many do you expect to get?

knows: reading short labels and comparing simple counts
doesNotKnow: that covering a note and rebuilding it from memory shows which details are missing, which reading it through cannot

misconception: Rereading a complete-looking note shows whether you know it.
objective: Reconstruct a missing field from a short source note.

claims.text: Scenario, hook and prediction: Cover it and rebuild its three fields: how many do you expect to get? Your note looks complete. Cover it and rebuild its three fields: how many do you expect to get? Correct option: Can't tell until you try. All fixture labels, example words, dates, task durations and file fields are stipulated exercise data.

claims.text: Stage: the card (room → B4, day → Friday, code → 627) shows at the prediction and is covered after it (room → ?, day → ?, code → ?). Each answer box starts empty and cycles through fixed choices (room: B4, D4, B6; day: Friday, Tuesday, Thursday; code: 672, 627, 267). Pressing each box once gives: Rebuilt 2 of 3. The readout “Note looks 3/3 filled” stands for the check made with everything in view. Reveal sentences: The note showed all three fields filled. Nothing was missing this time, and only rebuilding it could tell you that.

recall.question: Your meeting note has three fields: room, day and code. How do you find a value you do not actually know?
options: Cover the values and fill each field from memory
Reread the note slowly until it feels familiar
Check that each of the three fields has a value
recall.why: Reconstructing each value exposes the specific gap; a complete-looking note can still hide one you could not produce.
